title: Four-Fifths Bias Audit Calculator
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI-Native Schools
description: Calculate selection rates and four-fifths ratios for three student groups, decide which groups an audit flags, then change the counts and watch the flags update.

educational.topic: Screening an AI recommendation system for bias
learningObjectives: The learner will calculate selection rates and four-fifths ratios for three student groups and identify which groups the audit flags, correctly answering three of three questions.
prerequisites: Algorithmic bias, algorithmic bias auditing, selection rate, and the four-fifths rule, from the section "Algorithmic Bias, Auditing, and Transparency" in Chapter 10.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Commit three calculations before the sliders unlock, then explore the flags
keyQuestions: What is each group's selection rate?
commonMisconceptions: A flagged result proves the system is unfair
A group with the largest count must have the highest rate
A ratio is a difference in percentage points
assessmentOpportunities: Group B: 72 recommended of 300 eligible. Selection rate?
Group A's rate is 40.0%. Group B's ratio?
Group C's rate is 35.0%. Is it flagged?
Does a flag prove the system is unfair?

controls.name: Your answer box and Check
controls.description: type a number and press Check (or Enter); for question 3 choose from the menu. Two attempts per question; only the first counts.

controls.name: Next
controls.description: moves on; after question 3 it unlocks the sliders.

controls.name: Recommended, group A, B, C
controls.description: sliders for the number recommended in each group.

controls.name: Redo challenges and Defaults
controls.description: start the questions again, or reset the counts to 200, 72, and 70.
